pc-9-en: Should the monastic life be preserved with care and its authentic spirit permitted to shine forth ever more splendidly both in the East and the West?
pc-10-en: Is the religious life undertaken by lay people, either men or women, a state for the profession of the evangelical counsels which is complete in itself?
pc-11-en: Do Secular Institutes, although not Religious institutes, involve a true and full profession of the evangelical counsels in the world?
pc-12-en: Should the chastity for the sake of the kingdom of heaven which religious profess be counted an outstanding gift of grace?
pc-13-en: Should religious diligently practice, and if need be express also in new forms, that voluntary poverty which is an expression of the following of Christ?
pc-14-en: In professing obedience, do religious offer the full surrender of their own will as a sacrifice of themselves to God and so unite permanently to God's salvific will?
pc-15-en: Should common life, fashioned on the model of the early Church and given new force by the Gospel, the liturgy, and the Eucharist, continue to be lived in prayer and the communion of the same spirit?
pc-16-en: Should papal cloister be maintained for nuns engaged exclusively in the contemplative life, adjusted to conditions of time and place?
pc-17-en: Should the religious habit, an outward mark of consecration to God, be simple and modest, poor and at the same time becoming?
pc-18-en: Does adaptation and renewal of religious life depend greatly on the education of religious?
pc-19-en: When founding new religious communities, must their necessity or at least the many useful services they promise be seriously weighed?
pc-20-en: Should religious communities continue to maintain and fulfill the ministries proper to them, adapting them to the requirements of time and place?
pc-21-en: May the Holy See, after consulting local Ordinaries, forbid communities without reasonable hope of further development to receive novices and combine them with more flourishing ones?
pc-22-en: Should independent institutes and monasteries, when opportune and the Holy See permits, form federations if they belong to the same religious family?
pc-23-en: Does the synod favor conferences or councils of major superiors established by the Holy See?
pc-24-en: Should priests and Christian educators make serious efforts to foster religious vocations, corresponding to the needs of the Church?
pc-25-en: Should religious institutes respond generously to the specific vocation God gave them and to their work in the Church today?
po-1-en: In the renewal of Christ's Church, are tasks of the greatest importance and of ever increasing difficulty being given to the order of priests?
po-2-en: Has the Lord Jesus made his whole Mystical Body a sharer in the anointing of the Spirit with which he himself is anointed, so that all the faithful are a holy and royal priesthood?
po-3-en: Are priests taken from among men and ordained for men in the things that belong to God in order to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins, while living on earth with other men as brothers?
po-4-en: Since the People of God are joined together primarily by the word of the living God, do priests as co-workers with their bishops have the primary duty of proclaiming the Gospel of God to all?
po-5-en: Does God, who alone is holy and who alone bestows holiness, will to take as his companions and helpers men who humbly dedicate themselves to the work of sanctification?
po-6-en: Do priests, exercising the office of Christ the Shepherd and Head, gather the family of God together in the name of the bishop as a brotherhood enlivened by one spirit?
po-7-en: Do all priests, in union with bishops, share one and the same priesthood and ministry of Christ such that their consecration and mission require hierarchical communion with the order of bishops?
po-8-en: Are priests by virtue of their ordination united among themselves in an intimate sacramental brotherhood, forming one priesthood under their own bishop?
po-9-en: Though priests exercise the office of father and teacher among the People of God, are they nevertheless, together with all Christ's faithful, disciples of the Lord and sharers in his Kingdom?
po-10-en: Does the spiritual gift priests receive at ordination prepare them for the widest possible and universal mission of salvation, even to the ends of the earth?
po-11-en: Did Christ so constitute his Church that the people he acquired by his blood would have its priests to the end of time, and that Christians would never be like sheep without a shepherd?
po-12-en: Are priests made in the likeness of Christ the Priest by the Sacrament of Orders so that, collaborating with their bishops, they may build up and care for the Church as the Body of Christ?
po-13-en: Do priests who perform their duties sincerely and indefatigably in the Spirit of Christ arrive at holiness by this very fact?
po-14-en: Must priests, amid many obligations of office, coordinate and balance their interior life with outward activity rather than rely on mere external performance of the ministry?
po-15-en: Among the virtues needed for sacred ministry, is none so important for priests as readiness always to know and do the will of him who sent them and not their own will?
po-16-en: Is perfect and perpetual continence for the sake of the Kingdom of Heaven held by the Church to be of great value for the priestly life, to be embraced and esteemed as a gift?
po-17-en: By living in the world, should priests know how not to be of the world, esteeming created goods as gifts of God while practicing voluntary poverty?
po-18-en: Besides the exercise of their ministry, should priests use the common and particular means the Church commends for sanctification so as to grow in union with Christ?
po-19-en: Ought priests to be mature in knowledge, with doctrine that is spiritual medicine for the People of God, drawn especially from reading and meditating on sacred Scripture?
po-20-en: As those dedicated to the service of God, do priests deserve to receive an equitable remuneration, since the laborer is worthy of his hire?
po-21-en: Following the example of the early Church in Jerusalem who held all things in common, should common funds and a system of social assistance for priests be established?
po-22-en: While recognizing the joys of the priestly life, must the difficulties priests experience in contemporary economic, social, and cultural conditions also be kept in view?
sc-1-en: Does the sacred Council desire to impart increasing vigor to the Christian life of the faithful, adapt changeable institutions to present needs, foster union among believers in Christ, and strengthen what can call mankind into the Church?
sc-2-en: Is the liturgy, through which the work of our redemption is accomplished, especially in the divine sacrifice of the Eucharist, the outstanding means whereby the faithful express in their lives and manifest to others the mystery of Christ and the true Church?
sc-3-en: Should principles concerning the promotion and reform of the liturgy be called to mind, and practical norms established, some applying to the Roman rite and also to all other rites?
sc-4-en: Does holy Mother Church hold all lawfully acknowledged rites to be of equal right and dignity, wishing to preserve them and, where necessary, revise them carefully in the light of sound tradition?
sc-5-en: When the fullness of time had come, did God who wills that all men be saved send His Son, the Word made flesh, anointed by the Holy Spirit, to preach the gospel to the poor and heal the contrite of heart?
sc-6-en: Just as Christ was sent by the Father, did He also send the apostles, filled with the Holy Spirit, to preach the gospel to every creature and proclaim that by His death and resurrection He had freed us from Satan and death?
sc-7-en: Is Christ always present in His Church, especially in her liturgical celebrations, in the sacrifice of the Mass, under the Eucharistic species, in the sacraments, in His word, and when the Church prays and sings?
sc-8-en: In the earthly liturgy, do we take part in a foretaste of that heavenly liturgy celebrated in the holy city of Jerusalem toward which we journey as pilgrims, where Christ sits at the right hand of God?
sc-9-en: Before men can come to the liturgy, must they first be called to faith and to conversion, since the sacred liturgy does not exhaust the entire activity of the Church?
sc-10-en: Is the liturgy the summit toward which the activity of the Church is directed and, at the same time, the font from which all her power flows?
sc-11-en: For the liturgy to produce its full effects, must the faithful come to it with proper dispositions, minds attuned to their voices, and cooperation with divine grace?
sc-12-en: Is the spiritual life not limited solely to participation in the liturgy, since the Christian must also enter into his chamber to pray to the Father in secret and should pray without ceasing?
sc-13-en: Are popular devotions of the Christian people to be highly commended, provided they accord with the laws and norms of the Church, especially when ordered by the Apostolic See?
sc-14-en: Does Mother Church earnestly desire that all the faithful be led to that fully conscious and active participation in liturgical celebrations demanded by the very nature of the liturgy?
sc-15-en: Must professors appointed to teach liturgy in seminaries, religious houses of study, and theological faculties be properly trained in institutes which specialize in this subject?
sc-16-en: Is the study of sacred liturgy to be ranked among the compulsory and major courses in seminaries and religious houses of studies, and among the principal courses in theological faculties?
sc-17-en: Shall clerics in seminaries and houses of religious be given a liturgical formation in their spiritual life so they understand the sacred rites and take part in them wholeheartedly?
sc-18-en: Are priests already working in the Lord's vineyard to be helped to understand more fully what they do when they perform sacred rites, and to live and share the liturgical life with the faithful?
sc-19-en: Must pastors of souls promote with zeal and patience the liturgical instruction of the faithful and their active participation in the liturgy both internally and externally?
sc-20-en: Shall transmissions of the sacred rites by radio and television be done with discretion and dignity under the leadership of a suitable person appointed by the bishops?
sc-21-en: Does holy Mother Church desire to undertake with great care a general restoration of the liturgy, distinguishing immutable elements divinely instituted from elements subject to change?
sc-22-en: Does regulation of the sacred liturgy depend solely on the authority of the Church—the Apostolic See and, as laws may determine, the bishop—and within defined limits on competent territorial bodies of bishops?
sc-23-en: That sound tradition may be retained and legitimate progress remain open, must careful theological, historical, and pastoral investigation always be made into each part of the liturgy to be revised?
sc-24-en: Is sacred Scripture of the greatest importance in the celebration of the liturgy, as the source of lessons, psalms, prayers, and the meaning of liturgical actions and signs?
sc-25-en: Are the liturgical books to be revised as soon as possible, with experts employed on the task and bishops consulted from various parts of the world?
sc-26-en: Are liturgical services not private functions but celebrations of the Church, the sacrament of unity—the holy people united and ordered under their bishops?
sc-27-en: Whenever rites make provision for communal celebration with the presence and active participation of the faithful, is this way to be preferred, so far as possible, to individual and quasi-private celebration?
sc-28-en: In liturgical celebrations, should each person, minister or layman, who has an office to perform do all of, but only, those parts which pertain to his office by the nature of the rite and the principles of liturgy?
sc-29-en: Do servers, lectors, commentators, and members of the choir also exercise a genuine liturgical function requiring sincere piety, decorum, and training in the spirit of the liturgy?
sc-30-en: To promote active participation, should the people be encouraged to take part by acclamations, responses, psalmody, antiphons, and songs, as well as by actions, gestures, and bodily attitudes, and at proper times observe reverent silence?
sc-31-en: Must the revision of the liturgical books carefully attend to the provision of rubrics also for the people's parts?
sc-32-en: Apart from distinctions of liturgical function and sacred Orders, and due honors to civil authorities, may any special honors be paid in the liturgy to private persons or classes of persons?
sc-33-en: Although the sacred liturgy is above all things the worship of the divine Majesty, does it likewise contain much instruction for the faithful, as God speaks to His people and Christ proclaims His gospel?
sc-34-en: Should the rites be distinguished by a noble simplicity—short, clear, unencumbered by useless repetitions, within the people's powers of comprehension, and normally not requiring much explanation?
sc-35-en: That the intimate connection between words and rites may be apparent, is there to be more reading from holy Scripture in sacred celebrations, more varied and suitable, with preaching given its proper place?
sc-36-en: While particular law remains in force and Latin is to be preserved in the Latin rites, may the use of the mother tongue in the Mass, sacraments, and other parts of the liturgy be extended for the people's advantage?
sc-37-en: Even in the liturgy, does the Church wish to impose no rigid uniformity in matters which do not implicate the faith or the good of the whole community, but rather respect and foster the genius and talents of various peoples?
sc-38-en: When revising the liturgical books, shall provisions be made for legitimate variations and adaptations to different groups, regions, and peoples, especially in mission lands, provided the substantial unity of the Roman rite is preserved?
sc-39-en: Within the limits set by the typical editions of the liturgical books, does it belong to the competent territorial ecclesiastical authority to specify adaptations especially for sacraments, sacramentals, processions, liturgical language, sacred music, and the arts?
sc-40-en: Where an even more radical adaptation of the liturgy is needed, must the competent territorial ecclesiastical authority carefully consider which elements from peoples' traditions and culture might appropriately be admitted into divine worship?
sc-41-en: Is the bishop to be considered as the high priest of his flock, from whom the life in Christ of his faithful is in some way derived and dependent?
sc-42-en: Because the bishop cannot always preside over the whole flock, are parishes set up locally under a pastor who takes the place of the bishop the most important lesser groupings of the faithful?
sc-43-en: Is zeal for the promotion and restoration of the liturgy rightly held to be a sign of the providential dispositions of God in our time, as a movement of the Holy Spirit in His Church?
sc-44-en: Is it desirable that the competent territorial ecclesiastical authority set up a liturgical commission assisted by experts in liturgical science, sacred music, art, and pastoral practice?
sc-45-en: Is every diocese to have a commission on the sacred liturgy under the direction of the bishop for promoting the liturgical apostolate?
sc-46-en: Besides the commission on the sacred liturgy, should every diocese, as far as possible, have commissions for sacred music and sacred art, working in closest collaboration?
sc-47-en: At the Last Supper, on the night when He was betrayed, did our Saviour institute the eucharistic sacrifice of His Body and Blood to perpetuate the sacrifice of the Cross until He should come again?
sc-48-en: Does the Church earnestly desire that Christ's faithful, when present at this mystery of faith, not be strangers or silent spectators, but take part in the sacred action with devotion and full collaboration?
sc-49-en: For Masses celebrated with the assistance of the faithful, especially on Sundays and feasts of obligation, has the sacred Council made decrees so that the sacrifice of the Mass may become pastorally efficacious to the fullest degree?
sc-50-en: Is the rite of the Mass to be revised so that the nature and purpose of its parts and the connection between them may be more clearly manifested, and devout and active participation by the faithful more easily achieved?
sc-51-en: Are the treasures of the Bible to be opened up more lavishly, so that richer fare may be provided for the faithful at the table of God's word over a prescribed number of years?
sc-52-en: Is the homily, by which the mysteries of the faith and the guiding principles of Christian life are expounded from the sacred text, to be highly esteemed as part of the liturgy itself and not omitted on Sundays and feasts of obligation?
sc-53-en: Especially on Sundays and feasts of obligation, is the common prayer or prayer of the faithful to be restored after the Gospel and the homily, with intercession for the Church, civil authorities, those in need, and the salvation of the world?
sc-54-en: In Masses celebrated with the people, may a suitable place be allotted to their mother tongue, especially for the readings and the common prayer, while steps are taken so that the faithful may also say or sing in Latin those parts of the Ordinary that pertain to them?
sc-55-en: Is that more perfect form of participation in the Mass whereby the faithful, after the priest's communion, receive the Lord's body from the same sacrifice strongly commended?
sc-56-en: Are the liturgy of the word and the eucharistic liturgy so closely connected that they form but one single act of worship, so that the faithful should take their part in the entire Mass?
sc-57-en: Has concelebration, whereby the unity of the priesthood is appropriately manifested, remained in use in the Church both in the East and in the West, and is permission for it to be extended?
sc-58-en: Is a new rite for concelebration to be drawn up and inserted into the Pontifical and into the Roman Missal?
sc-59-en: Is the purpose of the sacraments to sanctify men, to build up the body of Christ, and to give worship to God, and because they are signs do they also instruct?
sc-60-en: Has holy Mother Church instituted sacramentals as sacred signs resembling the sacraments, signifying spiritual effects obtained through the Church's intercession?
sc-61-en: For well-disposed members of the faithful, does the liturgy of the sacraments and sacramentals sanctify almost every event in their lives, giving access to the stream of divine grace flowing from the paschal mystery?
sc-62-en: Have certain features crept into the rites of the sacraments and sacramentals which have rendered their nature and purpose far from clear, so that some changes have become necessary to adapt them to present needs?
sc-63-en: Because the mother tongue in administering the sacraments and sacramentals can often help the people, is this use to be extended according to the norms of the Constitution?
sc-64-en: Is the catechumenate for adults, comprising several distinct steps, to be restored and taken into use at the discretion of the local ordinary?
sc-65-en: In mission lands, may elements from peoples' initiation rites, when capable of being adapted to Christian ritual, be admitted along with those already found in Christian tradition?
sc-66-en: Are both the simpler and the more solemn rites for the baptism of adults to be revised, taking into account the restored catechumenate?
sc-67-en: Is the rite for the baptism of infants to be revised and adapted to the circumstance that those to be baptized are in fact infants, bringing out more clearly the roles of parents and godparents?
sc-68-en: Should the baptismal rite contain variants for occasions when a very large number are to be baptized together, and a shorter rite for mission lands and danger of death when no priest or deacon is available?
sc-69-en: In place of the rite for supplying what was omitted in the baptism of an infant, is a new rite to be drawn up that more clearly manifests that the infant has already been received into the Church?
sc-70-en: Except during Eastertide, may baptismal water be blessed within the rite of baptism itself by an approved shorter formula?
sc-71-en: Is the rite of confirmation to be revised so that its intimate connection with the whole of Christian initiation is more clearly set forth, with candidates renewing their baptismal promises just before confirmation?
sc-72-en: Are the rite and formulas for the sacrament of penance to be revised so that they more clearly express both the nature and effect of the sacrament?
sc-73-en: Is extreme unction, which may more fittingly be called anointing of the sick, a sacrament not only for those at the point of death, but fitting as soon as any of the faithful begins to be in danger of death from sickness or old age?
sc-74-en: Besides separate rites for anointing of the sick and for viaticum, shall a continuous rite be prepared in which the sick person is anointed after confession and before receiving viaticum?
sc-75-en: Is the number of the anointings to be adapted to the occasion, and are the prayers of the rite of anointing to be revised to correspond with the varying conditions of the sick?
sc-76-en: Are both the ceremonies and texts of the ordination rites to be revised, with the bishop's address possibly in the mother tongue and the laying of hands at a bishop's consecration done by all bishops present?
sc-77-en: Is the marriage rite in the Roman Ritual to be revised and enriched so that the grace of the sacrament is more clearly signified and the duties of the spouses are taught?
sc-78-en: Is matrimony normally to be celebrated within the Mass, after the gospel and homily and before the prayer of the faithful?
sc-79-en: Are the sacramentals to undergo a revision that enables the faithful to participate intelligently, actively, and easily, considering also the circumstances of our own days?
sc-80-en: Is the rite for the consecration of virgins in the Roman Pontifical to be revised, and a rite of religious profession and renewal of vows drawn up for greater unity, sobriety, and dignity?
sc-81-en: Should the rite for the burial of the dead express more clearly the paschal character of Christian death and correspond more closely to the circumstances and traditions of various regions?
sc-82-en: Is the rite for the burial of infants to be revised, and a special Mass for the occasion provided?
sc-83-en: Did Christ Jesus, high priest of the new and eternal covenant, introduce into this earthly exile that hymn sung throughout all ages in the halls of heaven, joining the entire community of mankind to Himself in this canticle of divine praise?
sc-84-en: By tradition going back to early Christian times, is the divine office devised so that the whole course of the day and night is made holy by the praises of God?
sc-85-en: Do all who render the service of the divine office not only fulfill a duty of the Church but also share in the greatest honor of Christ's spouse, standing before God's throne in the name of the Church?
sc-86-en: Will priests engaged in the sacred pastoral ministry offer the praises of the hours with greater fervor the more vividly they realize that they must heed St. Paul's exhortation to pray without ceasing?
sc-87-en: In order that the divine office may be better and more perfectly prayed in existing circumstances, has the sacred Council seen fit to decree concerning the office of the Roman rite?
sc-88-en: Because the purpose of the office is to sanctify the day, is the traditional sequence of the hours to be restored so that they may be genuinely related to the time of day when they are prayed?
sc-89-en: When the office is revised, are Lauds as morning prayer and Vespers as evening prayer to be considered the chief hours, the two hinges on which the daily office turns?
sc-90-en: Because the divine office is the public prayer of the Church, is it a source of piety and nourishment for personal prayer, so that those who take part should attune their minds to their voices?
sc-91-en: So that the course of the hours may be observable in practice, are the psalms no longer to be distributed throughout one week but through some longer period of time?
sc-92-en: In the divine office, shall readings from sacred Scripture be arranged so that the riches of God's word may be easily accessible in more abundant measure, with better selection from the fathers and authentic lives of the saints?
sc-93-en: To whatever extent may seem desirable, are the hymns of the office to be restored to their original form, removing whatever smacks of mythology or ill accords with Christian piety?
sc-94-en: That the day may be truly sanctified, is it best that each hour be prayed at a time which most closely corresponds with its true canonical time?
sc-95-en: Are communities obliged to choral office bound to celebrate the office in choir every day in addition to the conventual Mass?
sc-96-en: Are clerics not bound to office in choir, if they are in major orders, bound to pray the entire office every day, either in common or individually?
sc-97-en: Are appropriate instances to be defined by the rubrics in which a liturgical service may be substituted for the divine office, and may ordinaries for a just reason dispense from or commute the obligation?
sc-98-en: Do members of an institute dedicated to acquiring perfection who, according to their constitutions, recite any parts of the divine office thereby perform the public prayer of the Church?
sc-99-en: Since the divine office is the voice of the Church publicly praising God, are clerics not obliged to choir, especially priests who live together, urged to pray at least some part of the office in common?
sc-100-en: Should pastors of souls see to it that the chief hours, especially Vespers, are celebrated in common in church on Sundays and the more solemn feasts, and are the laity also encouraged to recite the divine office?
sc-101-en: In accordance with the centuries-old tradition of the Latin rite, is the Latin language to be retained by clerics in the divine office, though the ordinary may grant a vernacular version in individual cases of grave obstacle?
sc-102-en: Must holy Mother Church celebrate the saving work of her divine Spouse by devoutly recalling it on certain days throughout the year, keeping the Lord's resurrection every Sunday and at Easter?
sc-103-en: In celebrating the annual cycle of Christ's mysteries, does holy Church honor with especial love the Blessed Mary, Mother of God, who is joined by an inseparable bond to the saving work of her Son?
sc-104-en: Has the Church also included in the annual cycle days devoted to the memory of the martyrs and the other saints, who sing God's perfect praise in heaven and offer prayers for us?
sc-105-en: In the various seasons of the year, does the Church complete the formation of the faithful by pious practices for soul and body, by instruction, prayer, and works of penance and of mercy?
sc-106-en: By apostolic tradition originating from the day of Christ's resurrection, does the Church celebrate the paschal mystery every eighth day—the Lord's day—when the faithful come together to hear the word of God and take part in the Eucharist?
sc-107-en: Is the liturgical year to be revised so that the traditional customs and discipline of the sacred seasons are preserved or restored to suit modern conditions, retaining their specific character and nourishing piety centered on the paschal mystery?
sc-108-en: Must the minds of the faithful be directed primarily toward the feasts of the Lord whereby the mysteries of salvation are celebrated, with the proper of the time preferred over the feasts of the saints?
sc-109-en: Does the season of Lent have a twofold character—recalling or preparing for baptism and by penance disposing the faithful to celebrate the paschal mystery—and is this to be brought into greater prominence in the liturgy and catechesis?
sc-110-en: During Lent, should penance be not only internal and individual, but also external and social, while the paschal fast is kept sacred?
sc-111-en: Have the saints been traditionally honored in the Church and their authentic relics and images held in veneration, while many feasts of the saints are left to celebration by a particular Church or nation or religious family lest they take precedence over the mysteries of salvation?
sc-112-en: Is the musical tradition of the universal Church a treasure of inestimable value, greater even than that of any other art, forming a necessary or integral part of the solemn liturgy?
sc-113-en: Is liturgical worship given a more noble form when the divine offices are celebrated solemnly in song, with the assistance of sacred ministers and the active participation of the people?
sc-114-en: Is the treasure of sacred music to be preserved and fostered with great care, with choirs diligently promoted and the whole body of the faithful enabled to contribute their active participation?
sc-115-en: Is great importance to be attached to the teaching and practice of music in seminaries, novitiates and houses of study of religious, and other Catholic institutions and schools?
sc-116-en: Does the Church acknowledge Gregorian chant as specially suited to the Roman liturgy and, other things being equal, should it be given pride of place in liturgical services, without excluding other kinds of sacred music such as polyphony?
sc-117-en: Is the typical edition of the books of Gregorian chant to be completed, and a more critical edition prepared of those books already published since the restoration by St. Pius X?
sc-118-en: Is religious singing by the people to be intelligently fostered so that in devotions, sacred exercises, and liturgical services the voices of the faithful may ring out according to the norms of the rubrics?
sc-119-en: In mission lands and elsewhere, where peoples have their own musical traditions that play a great part in their religious and social life, is due importance to be attached to their music in adapting worship to their native genius?
sc-120-en: In the Latin Church, is the pipe organ to be held in high esteem as the traditional instrument that adds splendor to the Church's ceremonies and lifts up man's mind to God, while other suitable instruments may also be admitted?
sc-121-en: Should composers cultivate sacred music and produce compositions proper to genuine sacred music, providing also for small choirs and the active participation of the entire assembly of the faithful?
sc-122-en: Do the fine arts rank among the noblest activities of man's genius, and is this especially true of religious art and its highest achievement, sacred art, oriented toward the infinite beauty of God?
sc-123-en: Has the Church admitted styles of art from every period according to the natural talents and circumstances of peoples and the needs of the various rites, rather than adopting any particular style as her very own?
sc-124-en: Should ordinaries, by the encouragement they show to art which is truly sacred, strive after noble beauty rather than mere sumptuous display, also in sacred vestments and ornaments?
sc-125-en: Is the practice of placing sacred images in churches so that they may be venerated by the faithful to be maintained, while their number should be moderate and their relative positions reflect right order?
sc-126-en: When passing judgment on works of art, shall local ordinaries give a hearing to the diocesan commission on sacred art and other experts, and carefully see that sacred furnishings and works of value are not disposed of or dispersed?
sc-127-en: Should bishops have a special concern for artists, so as to imbue them with the spirit of sacred art and of the sacred liturgy?
sc-128-en: Along with the revision of the liturgical books, is there to be an early revision of the canons and ecclesiastical statutes governing the provision of material things involved in sacred worship?
sc-129-en: During their philosophical and theological studies, are clerics to be taught about the history and development of sacred art and the sound principles governing the production of its works?
sc-130-en: Is it fitting that the use of pontificals be reserved to those ecclesiastical persons who have episcopal rank or some particular jurisdiction?
ur-1-en: Is the restoration of unity among all Christians one of the principal concerns of the Church, since Christ the Lord founded one Church and one Church only?
ur-2-en: Has what revealed the love of God among us been that the Father sent into the world His only-begotten Son, so that being made man He might by His redemption give new life to the entire human race and unify it?
ur-3-en: Even in the beginnings of the one and only Church of God, did certain rifts arise which the Apostle strongly condemned, and in later centuries more serious dissensions separate large communities from full communion with the Catholic Church?
ur-4-en: Under the inspiring grace of the Holy Spirit, should the Catholic faithful recognize the signs of the times and take an active and intelligent part in the work of ecumenism?
ur-5-en: Is the attainment of union the concern of the whole Church, faithful and shepherds alike, according to each one's talent?
ur-6-en: Is every renewal of the Church essentially grounded in an increase of fidelity to her own calling, and is this the basis of the movement toward unity?
ur-7-en: Can there be ecumenism worthy of the name without a change of heart, renewal of the inner life, self-denial, and unstinted love?
ur-8-en: Should change of heart and holiness of life, along with public and private prayer for the unity of Christians, be regarded as the soul of the whole ecumenical movement—spiritual ecumenism?
ur-9-en: Must Catholics get to know the outlook of their separated brethren through study pursued with realism and good will, including their doctrines, history, spiritual and liturgical life?
ur-10-en: Must sacred theology and other branches of knowledge, especially of a historical nature, be taught with due regard for the ecumenical point of view, so that they may correspond more exactly with the facts?
ur-11-en: Should the way and method in which the Catholic faith is expressed never become an obstacle to dialogue with separated brethren, while doctrine is clearly presented in its entirety without false irenicism?
ur-12-en: Before the whole world, should all Christians confess their faith in the triune God and the incarnate Son of God, and united in their efforts with mutual respect bear witness to their common hope?
ur-13-en: Did the first divisions in the East arise when the dogmatic formulae of Ephesus and Chalcedon were challenged, and later when communion between the Eastern Patriarchates and the Roman See was dissolved?
ur-14-en: For many centuries, did the Church of the East and that of the West follow their separate ways though linked in a brotherly union of faith and sacramental life, with the Roman See by common consent acting as guide when disagreements arose?
ur-15-en: Do the Christians of the East celebrate the sacred liturgy, especially the eucharistic celebration, with great love as source of the Church's life and pledge of future glory, entering into communion with the most holy Trinity?
ur-16-en: From the earliest times, have the Eastern Churches followed their own forms of ecclesiastical law and custom, sanctioned by the Fathers, synods, and even ecumenical councils, such diversity adding to the Church's splendor rather than obstructing unity?
ur-17-en: Must what is said about lawful variety in the Church also apply to differences in theological expression of doctrine, since East and West have followed different methods in the study of revelation?
ur-18-en: For the restoration or maintenance of unity and communion, is it necessary to impose no burden beyond what is essential?
ur-19-en: In the upheaval that began in the West toward the end of the Middle Ages and in later times, did Churches and ecclesial Communities come to be separated from the Apostolic See of Rome, while retaining a particularly close affinity with the Catholic Church?
ur-20-en: Do those Christians who make open confession of Jesus Christ as God and Lord and as the sole Mediator between God and men, to the glory of the one God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, hold a place of first concern in ecumenical reflection?
ur-21-en: Does a love and reverence of Sacred Scripture which might be described as devotion lead separated brethren to a constant meditative study of the sacred text?
ur-22-en: Whenever Baptism is duly administered as Our Lord instituted it and received with the right dispositions, is a person truly incorporated into the crucified and glorified Christ and reborn to a sharing of the divine life?
ur-23-en: Is the daily Christian life of these brethren nourished by their faith in Christ and strengthened by the grace of Baptism and by hearing the word of God?
ur-24-en: Must the faithful refrain from superficiality and imprudent zeal which can hinder real progress toward unity, while their ecumenical action remains fully and sincerely Catholic and faithful to the truth?
con3-exposition-p1-en: Is the only Son and Word of God the Father, who became a man like us in all things but sin, Christ our true God, the light of the world as he proclaimed in the gospel?
con3-exposition-p2-en: Does this holy and universal synod, driving afar the error of impiety, follow without deviation the holy and accepted fathers and accord in all things with the five holy and universal synods?
con3-exposition-p3-en: Has this holy and universal synod, reaffirming the divine tenets of piety unaltered and banishing profane teachings of impiety, set its seal on the creed made by the 318 fathers and confirmed by the 150?
con3-exposition-p4-en: Do the faithful believe in one God as confessed in the Creed of Nicaea and of Constantinople I?
con3-exposition-p6-en: Was the pious and orthodox creed of the divine favour enough for a complete knowledge of the orthodox faith and a complete assurance therein?
con3-exposition-p7-en: Has Christ our God stirred up the faithful emperor as a new David to gather this holy assembly so that it might find the perfect proclamation of right belief?
con3-exposition-p8-en: Does this holy and universal synod faithfully accept and welcome the report of Agatho, most holy and most blessed pope of elder Rome?
